podcast.body: Lou Reed released a solo album in 1972 that reportedly "confused his record company." This occurred after he ended his two-year self-imposed exile at his parents' house on Long Island, where he had been quietly writing poetry since leaving The Velvet Underground. "There was a solo album in 1972 that kind of confused his record company, but Bowie saw lots of potential."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album was released very quickly after the Velvet Underground's separation, heavily utilizing material that had been discarded by the Velvet Underground. Many of its themes also appear in unreleased Velvet Underground editions, with both VU versions and Lou Reed's solo versions of the exact same songs existing. While it received a relatively acceptable critical reception, it wasn't considered incredible and did not sell well, having little impact except for catching the attention of David Bowie. "Ese albún en solitario sale muy rápido porque si usaría muchísimo del material que había quedado desechado de la Belbet Underground."
